heading: China 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit 2026: 57 Countries, 65 Ports & 10-Day Rules
title: China 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit 2026: 57 Countries, 65 Ports & 10-Day Rules
description: Check China's 240-hour visa-free transit policy for 2026: 57 eligible countries, 65 designated ports, the 10-day clock, permitted areas, route rules, and common refusal risks.
quickAnswer: As reviewed in September 2026, nationals of 57 countries may apply for China's 240-hour visa-free transit when traveling from one country or region through mainland China to a different country or region. They need an ordinary passport, confirmed onward travel, a designated entry port, and an itinerary inside the permitted stay area. The National Immigration Administration states that the 240-hour clock starts at 00:00 on the day after entry. Meeting the published conditions allows an application for temporary entry; admission is not automatic.

contentSections.title: What changed on August 20, 2026
items: The National Immigration Administration added Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam on August 20, 2026, increasing the eligible nationality list from 55 to 57 countries.
The policy currently uses 65 designated entry ports across 24 provincial-level regions. The port count had increased from 60 to 65 on November 5, 2025, when five Guangdong ports were added.
The maximum stay is 240 hours, or 10 full 24-hour periods. It replaced the older 72-hour and 144-hour windows; 144 hours equals six days, while 240 hours equals ten days.
This remains a transit policy, not a general 10-day tourist visa waiver. The international journey must follow country or region A to mainland China to a different country or region B.
Travel, business, visits, and family visits may be permitted. Work, study, journalism, and other activities requiring prior approval still require the appropriate visa.

Policy data and nationality changes on this page were reviewed against National Immigration Administration sources in September 2026. Travelers should verify the exact route again before purchase and departure.

items: The table identifies the 65 designated entry ports in the current NIA policy. It does not mean travelers may enter through any international airport or travel anywhere in mainland China.
Read the port together with its permitted stay area. Some areas cover an entire province, while Shanxi, Heilongjiang, Jiangxi, Guangxi, Sichuan, and Yunnan are limited to named cities or prefectures.
Confirm the exit arrangement, onward ticket, and every domestic stop with the latest NIA table or the China Immigration Service hotline 12367 before booking.

contentSections.title: How the 10-day clock is calculated
items: The official 240-hour count begins at 00:00 on the day after immigration records the entry. The arrival day is not Day 1 of the 240-hour clock.
Example: if immigration records entry at 14:30 on May 1, the 240-hour period begins at 00:00 on May 2.
Ten complete 24-hour periods then run through May 11, with the 240-hour point reached at 00:00 on May 12.
The traveler should depart before the exact deadline recorded by immigration. Flight delays, airport transfers, security, and exit formalities require a practical buffer.
Do not calculate from the aircraft landing time or assume an extra partial day. Follow the temporary-entry record and ask the border inspection authority if the deadline is unclear.

contentSections.title: Three common rejection reasons
items: No confirmed onward ticket to a third country or region: an open ticket, standby plan, or return to the same country does not establish the required transit route.
Wrong port: the planned entry point is not one of the 65 designated ports, or the traveler cannot satisfy the port's temporary-entry procedure and onward arrangement.
Permitted-area violation: the itinerary includes a city or domestic transport segment outside the official area linked to the entry port.

Even when these three problems are avoided, temporary entry is decided by immigration inspection at the port. Carry the ordinary passport, onward booking, accommodation details, and evidence of entry permission for the next destination.

faqs: Who qualifies for China's 240-hour visa-free transit?

Nationals of the 57 countries listed by China's National Immigration Administration may apply when holding an ordinary passport and confirmed onward travel from one country or region through mainland China to a different country or region. They must use a designated port, remain in permitted areas, and satisfy immigration inspection.
How is the 240-hour visa-free period counted?

The National Immigration Administration states that the clock begins at 00:00 on the day after entry, not at landing time. If entry is recorded on May 1, counting begins at midnight starting May 2. Always follow the exact departure deadline recorded by immigration and leave a practical travel buffer.
Can I leave the airport transit area during the 240 hours?

Yes, if immigration grants temporary entry under the 240-hour policy. You may leave the port and travel inside the permitted stay area linked to your designated entry port. You cannot travel anywhere in mainland China automatically, and admission remains subject to inspection, documents, tickets, and route conditions.
